name: Rollout stability for rectified-flow 2D video forecaster

description: BASELINE: decoupled Gaussian pixel-noise context aug (TECHNIQUE=pixnoise, SIGMA=0.4). Reproduces user's finding: pixel noise fails on structured image data — sharpness_ratio=0.27 (very blurry, ideal 1.0), mass_drift=0.59. This is the bar to beat.

asi.hypothesis: Pixel-noise context aug is the known-weak baseline for image data; should reproduce blur/mass-drift failure
asi.setup: 2D video, IMG=32, C=1, K=2 ctx, Lorenz-driven blob, RF x-pred 1/(1-t)^2 weighted, 2000 train steps
asi.finding: Confirmed: pixnoise mmd=0.40, sharpness 0.27 (blurry), mass_drift 0.59. Noise floor mmd_floor~3e-4 (healthy). 64s/run.
asi.next: Try blur (known to help per user) — should beat this and validate benchmark

name: Rollout stability for rectified-flow 2D video forecaster (energy distance)

description: BASELINE (re-metric): pixnoise, now measured with energy distance (non-saturating). rollout_ed=9770, ed_late=15570. Metric switched because Gaussian-kernel MMD saturated identically at 0.404 for both pixnoise and blur.

asi.finding: Switched primary metric from Gaussian-kernel MMD (saturated at 0.404 for both pixnoise and blur — k_ab->0, mbb->1 ceiling) to ENERGY DISTANCE which is non-saturating. pixnoise ED=9770, ed_late=15570 (late drifts worse - good temporal signal), ed_floor=0 (healthy). huge dynamic range now.
asi.metric_history: MMD saturated identically (0.404124) for pixnoise AND blur -> useless. Energy distance fixes this.
asi.next: Run blur to confirm metric now discriminates (should differ from pixnoise). Then iterate techniques.

description: blur context aug BLUR_SIGMA=0.8: ED 9770->5214 (-47%), ed_late 15570->6240. Reproduces user finding that blur beats pixel noise. Cost: train_loss 0.16->3.37 (blur degrades condition), sharpness 1.65 (slight artifacts).

asi.finding: Blur(0.8) ED=5214 vs pixnoise 9770 (-47%). ed_late 6240 vs 15570. Confirms benchmark reproduces user's real-world finding: blur >> pixel noise for image rollout stability. BUT sharpness=1.65 (>1=artifacty) and train_loss=3.37 (blur degrades condition, harder to learn dynamics). Tradeoff: stability up, precision down + slight artifacts.
asi.next: Try smaller blur sigma (0.5) for better dynamics learning; then novel techniques (selffeed scheduled sampling, manifold_noise) to beat blur without the artifact/precision cost

description: selffeed (scheduled sampling, prob=0.3) + mild blur 0.4: ED 5214->725 (7x better than blur, 13x vs pixnoise). sharpness 0.88 (ideal!), mass_drift 0.08, train_loss 0.12 (low). Fixes blur's artifacts+precision loss. The principled exposure-bias fix wins decisively.

asi.finding: BREAKTHROUGH: selffeed (scheduled sampling) ED=725 vs blur 5214 (7x) vs pixnoise 9770 (13x). sharpness 0.88 (near ideal 1.0!), mass_drift 0.08, train_loss 0.12 (lower than pixnoise - model learns dynamics fine since mostly real data). Fixes ALL of blur's problems (artifacts 1.65, precision loss 3.37). This is THE technique for rollout stability.
asi.mechanism: Feeds model its own 1-step predictions as context during training (prob 0.3) + mild blur 0.4 -> directly closes train/inference gap. Principled exposure-bias fix.
asi.cost: wall 168s vs 65s (2.6x) due to extra sampling in train loop
asi.next: Tune selffeed prob; try pure selffeed without blur; test deeper rollout stability

description: DISCARD: pure selffeed (no blur). ED 725->1200, ed_late 906->2988. Mild blur on self-fed context is needed — smooths model errors.

asi.finding: Pure selffeed (no blur) WORSE: ED 725->1200, ed_late 906->2988. The mild blur (0.4) on self-fed predictions is important - it smooths model errors giving cleaner degraded contexts. Combo selffeed+mild-blur is the winner, not pure scheduled sampling.
asi.next: Tune selffeed prob up (0.5); maybe multi-step selffeed (2-step predictions) for deeper exposure

description: DISCARD: selffeed prob=0.5 too aggressive. ED 725->5869, ed_late 906->15739 (late divergence).

asi.finding: selffeed prob=0.5 MUCH worse: ED 725->5869, ed_late 906->15739 (diverges late, near pixnoise level). Too much self-feeding on early bad predictions harms dynamics learning. Sharp phase transition around prob 0.3-0.5. sharpness/mass still ok (0.83/0.09) but late rollout explodes -> compounding error sensitivity.
asi.next: Try prob=0.2 (less aggressive). Note: high run-to-run variance in ed_late due to chaotic rollout amplification - may need multi-seed confirmation of best config.

description: DISCARD: selffeed prob=0.2 ED=1410 (worse than 0.3). Optimum near 0.3.

asi.finding: selffeed prob=0.2 ED=1410 (worse than 0.3's 725). Bracket: 0.2->1410, 0.3->725, 0.5->5869. Optimum near 0.3. But single-run variance on chaotic rollout is high - need to confirm 0.3 reproduces.
asi.next: Re-run prob=0.3 to confirm 725 reproduces (not noise)

description: CONFIRM (discard dup): selffeed prob=0.3 reproduces ED=773 (vs 725 first). Robust.

asi.finding: CONFIRMED reproducible: selffeed prob=0.3 re-run ED=773 (first run 725), ed_late=1327. Robust ~7x better than blur. sharpness 0.78, mass_drift 0.14. Technique is real, not noise.

asi.finding: selffeed2 (2-step compounded) ED=988 WORSE than 1-step selffeed 725, ed_late 1695, and 280s wall (1.6x slower). Deeper compounding doesn't help - 1-step exposure is sufficient, compounded context is noisier. Optimum is single-step scheduled sampling.

description: selffeed_m (selffeed + on-manifold amplitude jitter): ED=747 (parity w/ selffeed within noise) + sharpness 0.78->0.90, mass_drift 0.14->0.07. Quality win at equal stability. New champion config.

On-manifold amplitude perturbation improves per-frame quality without hurting stability. Best overall config: sharp frames + stable rollout.
asi.config: TECHNIQUE=selffeed_m, SELFFEED_PROB=0.3, BLUR_SIGMA=1.0 (internal blur 0.4 + 8% amplitude jitter)
asi.next: Robustness: test on multichannel (C=2) and harder dynamics to confirm generalizes; write up findings

description: DISCARD: diff_forcing (per-frame pixel noise) ED=5540, sharpness 0.46. Fails like pixnoise - confirms all pixel-noise augs fail on image data.

asi.finding: diff_forcing (per-frame pixel noise) ED=5540, sharpness 0.46 - FAILS like pixnoise (only marginally better). Confirms: ALL pixel-noise-based context augmentation fails on structured image data regardless of schedule (pixnoise 9770, diff_forcing 5540). The noise TYPE matters more than the schedule. Only blur (structured) and selffeed (model-error) work.
asi.next: Curriculum selffeed: ramp p 0->0.3 over training to avoid early bad-prediction poisoning

description: DISCARD: curriculum selffeed (ramp 0->0.3) ED 747->2908. Reduces total exposure; early predictions don't poison. Constant p=0.3 is better.

asi.finding: Curriculum selffeed (ramp p 0->0.3 over 40%) WORSE: ED 747->2908, ed_late 9471, sharpness 0.55. Hypothesis (early bad predictions poison training) was WRONG - the ramp just reduces total self-feed exposure (avg p~0.21). Constant p=0.3 from start is better. Model benefits from MORE self-feed exposure, not less. Negative result, useful.
asi.next: Conclude - champion is selffeed_m (constant). Could try ramping DOWN or higher constant p with longer training, but diminishing returns.

description: DIAGNOSTIC: none (no aug) ED=5940. Shows pixnoise (9770) is WORSE than no-aug on slow image data - pixel noise actively harmful. selffeed_m 8x better than no-aug.

asi.finding: none (no aug) on default slow regime: ED=5940, sharpness 0.57. CRUCIAL: pixnoise (9770) is WORSE than no augmentation (5940) on slow/weather-like image data - pixel noise is actively HARMFUL, not just unhelpful. selffeed_m (747) is ~8x better than no-aug and ~13x better than pixnoise. Completes the regime story: augmentation is essential (none fails), but the WRONG augmentation (pixel noise) is worse than nothing on slow image data, while scheduled sampling is dramatically the best.
asi.regime_summary: slow/weather: none=5940, pixnoise=9770 (harmful!), blur=5214, selffeed_m=747. fast/chaotic: none=7336, pixnoise=438 (works), selffeed_m=931.

description: DISCARD: selffeed_m + inference blur 0.4. ED 747->1231. Inference-time blur hurts once scheduled sampling is in place.

asi.finding: selffeed_m + inference-time blur (0.4) HURTS: ED 747->1231, sharpness 0.90->0.73, ed_late 1051->2572. Once scheduled sampling handles stability, blurring clean rollout context is pure degradation. FINDINGS.md suggestion #3 (inference blur) does NOT compose with selffeed - it's only useful without scheduled sampling. Negative but useful: don't stack inference blur on selffeed.
asi.next: Loop has thoroughly explored the space (14 exps). Champion selffeed_m is robust. Could next try EMA-teacher surrogate or consistency loss but diminishing returns.

description: DISCARD: selffeed_ema_m (EMA teacher surrogate) ED 747->1218. Live model is the correct surrogate for scheduled sampling (matches inference distribution); lagging EMA is worse.

asi.finding: selffeed_ema_m (EMA teacher surrogate, decay 0.999) WORSE: ED 747->1218, ed_late 1051->2481, sharpness 0.90->0.76. Hypothesis (cleaner EMA surrogate) was WRONG. Reason: for scheduled sampling the LIVE model is the correct surrogate - at inference the model sees its own CURRENT predictions, so training on live-model predictions matches the inference distribution. A lagging EMA teacher (stale ~1000 steps behind) gives lower-quality contexts that mismatch inference. EMA teacher suits consistency DISTILLATION (stable target), not scheduled sampling (match own behavior).
asi.next: Try selffeed_m + spectral/TV regularizer (cheap, targets sharpness 0.90->1.0); distinct mechanism

description: DISCARD: selffeed_spec (spectral loss) ED=750 tied w/ champion 747, sharpness 0.81 slightly worse. Spectral regularizer doesn't help.

asi.finding: selffeed_spec (selffeed_m + spectral/TV HF-penalty loss, w=1e-2): ED=750.7 TIED with champion 747 (within noise), sharpness 0.81 slightly WORSE than 0.90. The one-sided Laplacian-energy penalty doesn't push sharpness to 1.0 and doesn't help ED. Champion selffeed_m robust against EMA-teacher and spectral-loss challenges.
asi.champion_status: selffeed_m (ED~747, sharpness 0.90) confirmed robust. Tried-and-failed additions: EMA teacher (1218), spectral loss (750 tie), curriculum (2908), 2-step (988), inference blur (1231), prob!=0.3 (worse).
asi.next: Try restart/noise-injection during ODE sampling (stochastic sampler) - distinct sampling-side mechanism attacking error compounding directly

description: selffeed_m BLUR_SIGMA=1.5 (internal blur 0.6): ED 747->285 (2.6x better!). ed_late 275<ed overall -> rollout stable end-to-end, no late divergence. New champion. Sharpness 1.11 (mild artifacts).

asi.finding: BREAKTHROUGH: stronger internal self-feed blur (BLUR_SIGMA=1.5 -> internal 0.6 vs old 0.4) ED 747->285 (2.6x better!). ed_late=275 LOWER than overall ed=285 -> rollout stable end-to-end, NO late divergence. mass_drift 0.05, train_loss 0.15. sharpness 1.11 (slightly over 1.0, mild artifacts - stronger blur pushes texture up). The internal blur on self-fed context is a key knob - sweeeping it found a much better operating point.
asi.mechanism: Stronger blur on the model's self-fed prediction smooths its errors MORE into plausible degraded contexts -> better robustness signal. Optimal is higher than the 0.4 I'd been using.
asi.next: Sweep BLUR_SIGMA further (1.2, 2.0) to find optimum and check sharpness tradeoff

CORRECTION: selffeed_m is ~750 at BLUR_SIGMA 1.0 (725/747/773) AND 1.5 (285-lucky/758) AND 1.3 (1145) - the blur sweep is WITHIN NOISE, no real improvement found. name: Rollout stability (deterministic regime) — reproducible single runs

description: BASELINE (deterministic regime): pixnoise ED=6746, sharpness 0.22. Deterministic mode makes runs reproducible (fixes the false-285 noise issue). ~20% slower but trustworthy.

Single runs now reproduce exactly (verified: selffeed_m gave 912.186462 twice). Cost: ~20% slower (170s->205s). All future comparisons are trustworthy.

Champion selffeed_m @ BLUR_SIGMA=1.0 = 912 (reproducible) stands.
asi.deterministic_resolution: Blur sweep: 1.0->912, 1.5->1015 (deterministic, reproducible). 1.0 wins. The non-deterministic 285/758/1145 were all noise.

asi.finding: selffeed_ms (selffeed_m + 2-step rollout loss, MS_PROB=0.3) DETERMINISTIC: ED 912->690 (-24%), ed_late 1240->710 (stable end-to-end), mass_drift 0.08->0.02, train_loss 0.19->0.08. Multi-step loss adds a loss term on predicting tgt2 from [ctx[:,1], model_pred(tgt)] - trains consistency over the model's OWN 2-step rollout, directly targeting compounding error. asi.next: RE-RUN identical config to confirm 690 reproduces (deterministic) before trusting

description: DISCARD: MS_DEPTH=3 ED 690->870, slower. 2-step is the sweet spot; deeper compounding adds noise. Champion depth=2 confirmed.

asi.finding: MS_DEPTH=3 (3-step rollout loss) WORSE: ED 690->870, ed_late 710->938, 371s wall. Deeper compounding (2 chained detached rollouts) gives noisier loss signal + slower. 2-step is the sweet spot (matches 'single-step suffices' pattern). Champion selffeed_ms (MS_DEPTH=2, MS_PROB=0.3, ED=690) confirmed optimal depth.
asi.next: Generalization check: does selffeed_ms (new champion) generalize to C=2 multichannel? (selffeed_m did, but the added 2-step loss could overfit)

description: DISCARD: selffeed_ms_grad (BPTT) ED 690->950, sharpness 0.75 (collapse). Detach is correct - gradient through prediction causes mode collapse. Validates champion.

asi.finding: selffeed_ms_grad (BPTT through multi-step loss, gradient-enabled pred1) WORSE: ED 690->950, sharpness 0.91->0.75 (mode-collapse signal), mass_drift 0.02->0.16, ed_late 710->1524. Gradient through the prediction rewards 'easy-to-predict-from' outputs -> partial collapse. DETACH is correct for both input-context selffeed AND the multi-step loss: decoupled training of tolerance/robustness beats coupled optimization. Validates champion design.
asi.design_principle: For scheduled-sampling / multi-step rollout loss, DETACH the model's own predictions. Gradient (BPTT) causes mode collapse. The detached version trains robustness; the gradient version rewards degenerate outputs.

description: TRAIN_STEPS=3500: ED 690->156 (4.4x), ed_late 710->157. Model was undertrained. Rollout ED compounds per-step gains. Candidate - re-confirming.

Mechanism: rollout stability is a COMPOUNDING measure - small per-step prediction improvements compound over 50 AR steps into large ED differences. train_loss only 0.08->0.10 (similar) but rollout ED 4.4x better. Legitimate (held-out eval, not overfitting). NEEDS re-confirmation (large gain, learned false-285 lesson).
asi.hypothesis: Model undertrained at 2000 steps; more training improves rollout stability super-linearly (compounding)

description: DISCARD: vae_noise (beta=1e-3,noise=0.5) ED=12712 (worse than pixnoise!), sharpness 0.22. VAE gives blurry corruptions -> same mean-regression failure as pixel noise.

asi.finding: vae_noise (VAE-latent corruption, beta=1e-3, noise=0.5) FAILED: ED 12712 (worse than pixnoise 6746!), sharpness 0.22 (same catastrophic blur as pixel noise). DIAGNOSIS: VAE recon is blurry + latent noise -> decoder regresses to mean -> corrupted contexts are blurry/mean-ish -> model learns mean regression (identical failure to pixel noise). KEY INSIGHT reaffirmed: self-feed works because model's own outputs are SHARP-but-slightly-wrong; blurry corruptions (pixel OR VAE) just teach blur. Need SHARP on-manifold corruption.
asi.next: Try sharp autoencoder (beta=1e-5, basically AE) + smaller noise (0.2) so corruptions stay sharp and on-manifold

description: DISCARD: vae_noise_blurj ED 1186->2077. Jitter over-corrupts with AE noise. Best no-self-feed VAE = vae_noise_blur (1186).

asi.finding: vae_noise_blurj (AE+blur+jitter) WORSE than vae_noise_blur: ED 1186->2077, sharp 0.93->0.78. Amplitude jitter over-corrupts on top of AE latent noise (unlike selffeed_m/manifold_noise where jitter helped). Best no-self-feed VAE variant = vae_noise_blur (AE-noise + mild blur, NO jitter), ED=1186, sharp 0.93.
asi.next: Get deterministic manifold_noise to complete no-self-feed comparison table for user

description: vae_noise_blur (sharp AE+blur) CONFIRMED ED=1186 reproducible. Best no-self-feed technique (5.7x pixnoise). Worse than selffeed_ms(690) which needs self-outputs.

asi.finding: vae_noise_blur (sharp AE beta=1e-5 + latent noise 0.2 + mild blur 0.4) CONFIRMED reproducible: ED=1186.483765 (both runs identical). sharpness 0.93, mass_drift 0.04. This is the BEST no-self-feed technique (simulates rollout drift via a learned AE, no model self-outputs needed - answers user's 4->3 fixed-dataset constraint). 5.7x better than pixnoise. Worse than selffeed_ms (690) which needs self-outputs the user can't make.
asi.no_self_feed_ranking: pixnoise 6746 (sharp 0.22) < vae_noise_blurry 12712 (FAILS, sharp 0.22) < manifold_noise 2142 (sharp 1.26 artifacty) < vae_noise_sharpAE 2113 (sharp 0.77) < vae_noise_blur 1186 (sharp 0.93) BEST. Champion selffeed_ms 690 (needs self-outputs).
asi.key_principle: VAE/latent corruption MUST be sharp: a normal VAE (KL>0) blurs -> fails like pixel noise (mean regression). Use a sharp AUTOENCODER (beta~0, recon_mse~5e-6) + small latent noise + mild blur.

asi.finding: VAE_NOISE=0.1 (gentler) ED=1600, worse than 0.2 (1186). Less latent-noise drift exposure -> less robustness learned. Curve: 0.1->1600, 0.2->1186. Try higher (0.3, 0.4) to find optimum.

description: DISCARD: VAE_NOISE=0.3 ED=2112. Sweep done: 0.2 optimal (1186). vae_noise_blur@0.2 = best no-self-feed.

asi.finding: VAE_NOISE=0.3 ED=2112 (worse), sharp 0.64 (off-manifold garbage). Sweep done: 0.1->1600, 0.2->1186 (OPTIMUM), 0.3->2112. Sharp valley at 0.2. vae_noise_blur@0.2=1186 confirmed best no-self-feed.

asi.finding: vae_interptemp_blur (temporal-neighbor latent interpolation + blur): ED=1305 (slightly worse than vae_noise_blur 1186 on primary) BUT BEST per-frame quality of any no-self-feed technique: sharpness 1.03 (near-ideal, vs noise's 0.93), mass_drift 0.006 (vs 0.04). Temporal interpolation = clean single-blob position shift (realistic rollout error), vs noise = off-manifold drift. TRADEOFF: noise wins rollout-ED, temporal-interp wins frame sharpness/mass. For weather (blurry=failure), temporal-interp's sharpness may be preferable.
asi.no_self_feed_final: Two strong no-self-feed options: vae_noise_blur (ED 1186, sharp 0.93) and vae_interptemp_blur (ED 1305, sharp 1.03, mass 0.006). Both need sharp AE. selffeed_ms=690 still champion if self-outputs possible.

description: DISCARD: vae_noise_blur@3500 ED=1419 (worse than 1186@2000). VAE corruption is STATIC (no compounding with training) vs selffeed CLOSED-LOOP (690->156). Why selffeed is structurally superior.

asi.finding: vae_noise_blur at TRAIN_STEPS=3500: ED=1419, WORSE than 1186 at 2000 steps (sharpness improved 0.93->0.99, mass 0.04->0.01, but ED worse). OPPOSITE of selffeed_ms (which improved 690->156 at 3500). FUNDAMENTAL DIFFERENCE: selffeed is CLOSED-LOOP (corruption = model's own improving predictions -> compounding gains with training); VAE corruption is STATIC (fixed AE) -> no compounding, even overfitting/instability (train_loss 0.14->0.64). This is WHY selffeed is structurally superior and why the VAE approach plateaus (~1186).
asi.implication: For the user: the VAE no-self-feed approach is capped (~1186, doesn't improve with training budget). Selffeed is fundamentally better (closed-loop). If the user can enable ANY self-feeding (even a tiny aux AR head), they get the compounding benefit.

description: DISCARD: CFG GUIDANCE=2.0 ED 690->2338, sharpness 1.28 artifacts. High guidance amplifies drifted context.

asi.finding: CFG (UNCOND_PROB=0.1, GUIDANCE=2.0) on champion WORSE: ED 690->2338, sharpness 1.28 (artifacts), mass 0.17, train_loss 0.35 (up). High guidance AMPLIFIES the (drifted) context signal -> artifacts. Also UNCOND_PROB=0.1 dilutes conditional training (future is highly context-determined, so unconditional prior is uninformative/broad). Try GUIDANCE<1 (blend toward unconditional to dampen bad context).
asi.next: GUIDANCE=0.5 test (dampen context reliance)

description: DISCARD: CFG GUIDANCE=0.5 ED=23827 catastrophic. CFG fails both directions - forecasting is context-determined so unconditional prior is uninformative. Last backlog mechanism tested.

asi.finding: CFG GUIDANCE=0.5 CATASTROPHIC: ED 23827 (vs 690), sharpness 0.38 (blurry), mass 0.47. Blending toward unconditional -> mean regression. CFG fails BOTH directions (2.0->artifacts/2338, 0.5->blur/23827). ROOT CAUSE: forecasting is highly context-determined (low aleatoric uncertainty) so unconditional prior is uninformative/broad. CFG suits high-uncertainty generation (t2i), not forecasting. Also UNCOND_PROB=0.1 itself hurts (train_loss 0.08->0.35) by diluting conditional training.
asi.conclusion: CFG = negative result. Technique space now EXHAUSTED: augmentations (selffeed wins), multi-step loss (2-step wins), VAE no-self-feed (sharp-AE noise+blur=1186 best proxy), CFG (fails), EMA/spectral/curriculum/inference-blur (all fail). Champion selffeed_ms=690 (156@3500).

description: GENERALIZATION (discard diag): N_BLOBS=2 multi-feature -> ranking REVERSES (pixnoise 1751 < selffeed_ms 2691). self-feed advantage is sparse-feature-specific; pixel noise OK on dense data (mean not degenerate).

asi.finding: REGIME REVERSAL on multi-feature data (N_BLOBS=2, 3 independent blobs): pixnoise ED=1751 (sharp 1.13) BEATS selffeed_ms ED=2691 (sharp 0.98). Opposite of single-blob (selffeed 690 vs pixnoise 6746). DEEP REASON: pixel-noise failure is specific to SPARSE-feature data where the data MEAN is degenerate (single blob -> mean is blank/blur -> catastrophic blur sharp 0.22). On DENSE multi-feature data the mean looks like valid data -> pixel noise is fine, AND self-feed backfires (hard task -> poor per-step predictions -> bad surrogate -> garbage self-fed contexts). selffeed train_loss 0.08(single)->0.32(multi) confirms harder task.
asi.caveat: self-feed recommendation is for SPARSE-feature data (isolated cells). For dense/full-field data (widespread precip), pixel noise is OK and self-feed's advantage shrinks/reverses. User's weather data regime matters: sparse->selffeed, dense->noise OK. Also self-feed hyperparams were tuned for single-blob; multi-blob optimum likely differs (less self-feed since predictions worse).
asi.data_structure_insight: The failure of pixel-noise augmentation = mean regression, which only catastrophically blurs when the data mean is degenerate (sparse features). Dense data is robust to it.

description: GENERALIZATION (discard diag): N_BLOBS=2 no-aug ED=1563 beats selffeed(2691) and pixnoise(1751). Self-feed helps sparse(8.6x) but hurts dense. Regime-specific recommendation.

asi.finding: N_BLOBS=2 no-aug (none): ED=1563 - BEST on multi-blob data (beats pixnoise 1751 AND selffeed_ms 2691). So self-feed HELPS 8.6x on sparse(single-blob: none 5940 -> selffeed 690) but HURTS on dense(multi-blob: none 1563 -> selffeed 2691, 1.7x worse). Augmentation of any kind hurts on dense/complex data. Mechanism: on hard/noisy tasks the model can't overfit clean conditions (less exposure bias) so augmentation isn't needed and adds noise; self-feed's poor surrogate (predictions bad on hard task) further hurts.
asi.regime_rule: Match technique to data regime: SPARSE features (isolated convective cells, the user's 'blurry cells' problem) -> self-feed helps a lot. DENSE features (widespread stratiform) -> no/aug or simple noise; self-feed may hurt. User's stated failure (blurry convective cells) is the sparse regime where self-feed wins.
asi.caveat: Strong self-feed recommendation is regime-specific (sparse predictable data). Multi-blob is artificial but the qualitative regime dependence is robust.

description: selffeed_msgate (error-gated, gate=0.5): ED 690->654 on sparse + fixes dense (2691->1822). Strict improvement, regime-robust. New champion candidate.

asi.finding: Error-gated self-feed (selffeed_msgate, gate=0.5 keep low-error half) STRICT IMPROVEMENT on sparse: ED 690->654, sharpness 0.91->0.97, mass_drift 0.02->0.009, ed_late 710->673. AND fixes dense regime (multi-blob 2691->1822, near pixnoise 1751). Gating cuts bad-surrogate self-feeds -> keeps good ones (sparse) while skipping when predictions poor (dense). REGIME-ROBUST technique. NEEDS re-confirm (deterministic).
asi.mechanism: Gate self-feed by surrogate accuracy: compute MSE(pred, real_ctx_frame) per sample, keep only low-error quantile. Adaptively self-feeds on easy/sparse data, skips on hard/dense - no sparsity detector needed.
asi.regimes: sparse single-blob: ungated 690 -> gated 654 (better). dense multi-blob: ungated 2691 -> gated 1822 (much better, near no-aug 1563).

description: CONFIRM (discard dup): selffeed_msgate gate=0.5 reproduces exactly 653.738220. Real. New champion.

asi.finding: CONFIRMED REPRODUCIBLE: selffeed_msgate gate=0.5 re-run = exactly 653.738220. Real. New champion ED=654 (was 690). Regime-robust (sparse 654, dense 1822).
asi.next: Sweep SELFFEED_GATE quantile (0.25 stricter, 0.75 looser) to find optimum

description: DISCARD: gate=0.25 ED=668 (>0.5's 654). Too strict. Optimum near 0.5.

asi.finding: gate=0.25 (stricter) ED=668, worse than 0.5 (654). Too few self-feeds on sparse loses the benefit. Curve: 0.25->668, 0.5->654, 1.0(ungated selffeed_ms)->690. Optimum near 0.5.
asi.next: gate=0.75 to confirm 0.5 is the peak

description: DISCARD: gate=0.75 ED=699. Sweep done: 0.5 optimal (654). selffeed_msgate gate=0.5 = new champion.

asi.finding: gate=0.75 ED=699 (worse). Sweep complete: 0.25->668, 0.5->654 (OPTIMUM), 0.75->699, 1.0(ungated)->690. Sharp peak at 0.5. Champion = selffeed_msgate gate=0.5, ED=654, regime-robust.

description: DISCARD: absolute error gate worse than quantile on dense (0.3->1917, 0.1->2004 vs quantile 1822). Biased subset. Quantile gate=0.5 remains champion (654).

asi.finding: Absolute error gate (err/frame_var) WORSE than quantile gate on dense: ABS=0.3->1917, ABS=0.1->2004 vs quantile 0.5->1822 (and no-aug 1563). Non-monotonic (stricter=worse). The absolute threshold keeps a BIASED subset (easy/predictable frames) that hurts more than a representative half. Quantile gate (relative, within-batch) is simpler and better. selffeed_msgate gate=0.5 (ED 654) remains champion.
asi.conclusion: Dense regime fundamentally hard to fix with self-feed (any self-feed hurts because predictions bad). Quantile gate=0.5 is the best compromise. Absolute gate abandoned.

description: DISCARD (budget point): gated@3500 ED=330 vs ungated@3500=156. Gating helps low-budget(654vs690@2000) but hurts high-budget. Budget-specific champion.

asi.finding: Gating benefit is BUDGET-DEPENDENT: gated@3500 ED=330 vs ungated@3500=156 (gating HURTS at high budget). But gated@2000=654 < ungated@2000=690 (gating HELPS at low budget). Mechanism: once well-trained, all surrogates are decent, so the gate discards USEFUL self-feed exposure -> reduces compounding. Gating is a regularizer that helps when model is noisy/undertrained, unnecessary/harmful at convergence.
asi.champion_budget_specific: TRAIN_STEPS=2000 -> selffeed_msgate (gated) ED=654. TRAIN_STEPS=3500 -> selffeed_ms (ungated) ED=156. Biggest lever remains training budget (closed-loop compounding). For the user: if training long, use ungated; if budget-limited, gated helps.
asi.note: 330 is a budget-increase point (vs 654@2000) AND worse than ungated@3500(156), so not a technique win. Standard regime stays selffeed_msgate@2000=654.

description: vae_ms (self-feed-free multi-step loss): ED 1186->1106. New best no-self-feed technique. Multi-step loss transfers to no-self-feed case via AE-corrupted real frames.

asi.finding: vae_ms (VAE context aug + SELF-FEED-FREE multi-step loss: predict t+1 from [ctx, AE-corrupt(real frame t)]) ED=1106, BETTER than vae_noise_blur (1186). The multi-step loss transfers to the no-self-feed case - training on a LOSS over a corrupted-context multi-step prediction helps (closes no-self-feed gap 1186->1106). Best no-self-feed technique. Sharpness 0.92, mass 0.05. Deterministic (reproducible).
asi.user_relevance: For the user's 4->3 / 7-frame constraint (can't self-feed): vae_ms is the best option. AE-corrupt the real frame t, use as drifted context, predict t+1 - emulates rollout drift as a LOSS without model self-outputs, using only frames they have (tgt, tgt2).
asi.no_self_feed_ranking: vae_ms 1106 (NEW BEST) > vae_noise_blur 1186 > vae_interptemp_blur 1305 > vae_noise 2113 > manifold 2142. Champion selffeed_msgate 654 (needs self-outputs).

description: BREAKTHROUGH (dense diag): vae_ms=821 on dense (confirmed) - beats all incl no-aug. Regime-robust (sparse 1106, dense 821). Self-feed fails dense; vae_ms doesn't. Reframes recommendation for mixed weather data.

asi.finding: BREAKTHROUGH: vae_ms is REGIME-ROBUST and excels on dense data! N_BLOBS=2 (dense): vae_ms=821 (confirmed reproducible) vs no-aug 1563, pixnoise 1751, selffeed_ms 2691, selffeed_msgate 1822. vae_ms BEATS EVERYTHING on dense including no-aug (1.9x). And it's regime-robust: sparse 1106, dense 821 (works on both, unlike self-feed which catastrophically fails on dense). asi.reframes_recommendation: For MIXED sparse/dense real weather data: vae_ms is the robust choice. Self-feed (sparse-only: 690 sparse but 2691 dense) fails on dense regions; vae_ms works everywhere. Even if self-feed is possible, for mixed/dense data vae_ms may be preferable overall. CORRECTS earlier 'augmentation hurts on dense' - only BAD aug (pixel noise, self-feed-bad-surrogate) hurts; on-manifold AE aug HELPS on dense.
asi.regime_table: sparse: selffeed_msgate 654 < vae_ms 1106 < no-aug 5940. dense: vae_ms 821 < no-aug 1563 < selffeed 2691. vae_ms robust on both.

asi.blur_sweep: BLUR_FRAC: 0.4->ED8801 sharp0.26(blurry), 0.5->ED1170 sharp0.97(ideal), 0.6->ED2141 sharp1.26(artifacty), 1.2->ED13682 sharp2.23. Sharp minimum ED near 0.5-0.6. More train blur -> model over-sharpens at inference.

asi.jitter_sweep: 0.04->ED1589 sharp1.13, 0.08->ED1170 sharp0.97, 0.12->ED988 sharp0.96. More jitter=better (down to 0.12). Try higher.

asi.tradeoff: jitter 0.16: ED921 sharp0.98 mass0.004 (ideal quality). jitter 0.20: ED730 sharp0.89 mass0.068 (lower ED but slightly blurry). User cares about sharpness (blurry=failure for weather cells).

description: DISCARD: manifold_noise @3500 steps ED=1373 (worse than 921@2000), train_loss 0.70. Static corruption plateaus/worsens with training (over-corrupts better model). Confirms structural limitation vs self-feed. Best at ~2000 steps.

UNLIKE self-feed (which compounded: 690@2000->156@3500 in old env).

asi.hypothesis: Corrupt ONLY the most-recent context frame (the slot holding the model's own output at inference), keep older real frames clean -> more realistic + better dynamics
asi.finding: MANIFOLD_LAST_ONLY=1, jitter=0.16: ED=824 (vs 921 corrupt-all), train_loss 0.11 (vs 0.13), ed_late 903 (vs 986). Better ED AND better dynamics (older clean frame gives accurate dynamics). Sharpness 1.11 (slightly artifacty). More realistic: at inference only recent frame is model output.

description: BEST CONFIG: manifold_noise LAST_ONLY=1 + jitter=0.20. ED=739, sharp=1.01 (ideal), mass_drift=0.001, ed_late=721. Last-frame-only corruption strictly beats all-frames on quality at equal ED.

Beats all-frames jitter0.20 (730 but sharp0.89 mass0.068) on EVERY quality metric at equal ED. Last-only corruption is strictly better.

description: selffeed_m (documented champion) = ED 1284 in current env — WORSE than manifold_noise LAST_ONLY (739). Self-feed env-specific; model outputs too degraded to feed back here. manifold_noise is champion AND user-applicable. Bank idea unnecessary.

In this harder/blurrier regime, the model's own outputs are too degraded to feed back productively. manifold_noise (simple static blur+jitter) BEATS selffeed. NO gap to close - the bank/pseudo-self-feed idea is unnecessary here.

In regimes where the model's per-step predictions are poor (hard dynamics, fast motion, undertrained), self-feed feeds bad surrogates and underperforms. Static on-manifold corruption (manifold_noise) is more robust. GREAT for user: the simple applicable technique (no self-feed needed) is also the BEST here.

description: ODE_STEPS=32 (inference sampling) -> ED=630, sharp 1.06. More accurate sampling reduces drift. Cheap (+2s). Note: 48 steps regresses to 1161 (chaotic), so 32 is the practical default, not a swept optimum.

asi.finding: ODE_STEPS=32 (inference) -> ED=630 (was 739 @16), sharp 1.06, +2s wall. More accurate per-step sampling -> less drift compounding. BUT ODE_STEPS=48 -> ED 1161 (WORSE) - chaotic non-monotonic sensitivity to discretization (16->739, 32->630, 48->1161). 32 is a sensible cheap default; beyond ~32 returns diminish/become noisy.
asi.caveat: Do NOT overfit by ODE_STEPS-sweeping the benchmark. 32 is justified as 'more accurate sampling', not as a tuned lucky point. The 48 regression shows the metric is chaotic w.r.t. inference discretization.

description: DISCARD: MANIFOLD_PROB=0.5 (mix clean+corrupt) -> ED 2609, worse. Must always corrupt (prob=1.0). Champion confirmed: manifold_noise LAST_ONLY always-corrupt + ODE_STEPS=32 = ED 630.

asi.finding: MANIFOLD_PROB=0.5 (mix clean+corrupted contexts) -> ED 2609, much WORSE than always-corrupt (630). The model must ALWAYS see corrupted context during training to learn deblurring - at inference it always sees its own degraded output. Mixing in clean samples dilutes the deblurring training -> blurrier rollout. MANIFOLD_PROB=1.0 (always) is correct.
asi.conclusion: Champion is final: manifold_noise LAST_ONLY + always-corrupt + ODE_STEPS=32. ED=630. Space thoroughly explored. Remaining variance is seed/data-scale (inherent, user tunes magnitude to their data).

description: DISCARD: 2nd-order samplers fail on x-pred RF. Heun@16 ED=22951 (velocity diverges at t=1 corrector); midpoint@16 ED=1781 (worse than Euler@16 739). Higher-order wrong for diverging v=(x-z)/(1-t). Euler@32 (630) is the sampling ceiling.

asi.hypothesis: 2nd-order ODE integrator (Heun/midpoint) for the RF sampler -> more accurate per-step -> less rollout drift
asi.finding: FAILED. Heun@16 -> ED 22951 (sharp 1.69, catastrophic): Heun's corrector evaluates velocity at t+dt=1.0 where v=(x-z)/(1-t) DIVERGES (clamped at /0.01 -> 100x blowup). Midpoint@16 -> ED 1781 (worse than Euler@16 739): even though midpoint avoids t=1, the 2nd-order assumption breaks on the diverging velocity field near t=1.
asi.conclusion: Higher-order integration is WRONG for x-prediction RF (velocity diverges as t->1). The sampling lever is MORE Euler steps (16->32 cut ED 739->630), not higher order. Euler@32 (630) is the sampling ceiling here. Reverting SAMPLER code.
asi.next_action_hint: Try a TRAINING-side principled idea: 'motion lag' corruption - blend the last context frame toward the previous frame (blob lags its true position), emulating the model's systematic under-prediction of motion. On-manifold (lagged position is a real past position). Combine with blur+jitter.

asi.hypothesis: Motion-lag corruption (blend last ctx frame toward previous, emulating model's motion under-prediction) would complement blur+jitter
asi.finding: FAILED. LAG=0.5 -> ED 1092 (train_loss 0.27); LAG=0.2 -> ED 1101 (train_loss 0.19). Both worse than champion 630 (train_loss 0.13). Lag consistently RAISES train_loss -> disrupts dynamics learning.
asi.key_principle: Only POSITION-PRESERVING corruptions work (blur, amplitude jitter). Position corruption (motion-lag here, spatial-shift earlier) breaks the temporal-position consistency the model needs to learn motion -> confuses dynamics. manifold_noise's blur+ampjitter preserve blob position, which is WHY they work. This sharply scopes the recommendation.

asi.finding: C=2 GENERALIZATION FAILS but for a MODEL reason, not the technique. C=2 baseline (none): ED 34661, sharp 1.92 (ARTIFACTS, not blur), train_loss 0.61 (model UNDERTRAINED on 2 channels - small ch=48/4-block model can't fit 2 channels in 2000 steps). manifold_noise@C=2 (j0.20): ED 57125 sharp 2.18 - WORSE. description: Champion @2500 steps -> ED 1076, train_loss 1.42 (DIVERGED). Instability cliff between 2000-2500 steps. 2000 is stable (reproduces exactly) but near the edge. Flags: for long training, monitor train_loss, use gentler LR/warmup. Toy's aggressive settings exaggerate this.

asi.finding: INSTABILITY CLIFF: champion @2500 -> ED 1076, train_loss 1.42 (vs 2000's 0.13). Training DIVERGES between 2000 and 2500 steps. The corruption + aggressive LR(2e-3) + velocity-weight-clamp(200) + cosine schedule makes optimization fragile beyond ~2000 steps in this toy.
asi.robustness_status: 2000 steps reproduces EXACTLY (629.59 twice) = stable operating point. But it's near the instability cliff. Beyond ~2000 the technique+training-setup gets shaky.
asi.implication_for_user: For long training runs: (1) the static corruption can destabilize optimization - monitor train_loss; (2) use a gentler LR / warmup / lower velocity-weight clamp for stability; (3) this toy's aggressive settings (LR 2e-3, no warmup) exaggerate the cliff - real weather training is usually more conservative. The PRINCIPLE (position-preserving context corruption) holds; the exact training schedule must ensure stability.

description: VEL_W_CLAMP trade-off: clamp=50 stabilizes long training (no divergence) but HURTS rollout quality (ED 1207 vs 630 @2000). High clamp=200 is load-bearing for sharp-endpoint prediction. Instability cliff is a genuine trade-off, not fixable by lowering clamp. Champion (clamp=200) is the quality optimum.

asi.finding: PARTIAL. clamp=50 STABILIZES training (2500-step train_loss 0.37 vs clamp=200's 1.42 divergence). BUT clamp=50 HURTS rollout quality: @2000 ED=1207 (vs clamp=200's 630), @2500 ED=1414. The high clamp (200) is LOAD-BEARING for rollout quality - it emphasizes the sharp near-data endpoint prediction. Lower clamp -> model fits velocity loss better (train_loss 0.036) but endpoint less sharp -> more rollout drift.
asi.conclusion: The >2000-step instability cliff is a genuine TRADE-OFF, not a fixable bug. clamp=200 optimizes rollout quality (sharp endpoint) but destabilizes long training with corruption. clamp=50 is stable but worse. Champion (clamp=200, @2000, ED=630) is the quality optimum. For the user: keep the high clamp for quality; control instability via LR/warmup/shorter-effective-corruption rather than the clamp.

Warmup is NOT a reliable lever here.

More capacity (ch=64, blocks=6) @C=2: still artifacts (sharp 1.78, train_loss 0.57) - NOT capacity-limited. The benchmark's C=2 setup is pathologically artifact-prone regardless of capacity/warmup/steps. Multichannel validation CANNOT be done in this toy - user must validate on their own well-behaved model.

description: NEGATIVE: EMA weight averaging doesn't help. decay 0.999 broken (init contamination, sharp 0.014); 0.99->651; 0.995->684 - all parity/worse than 630. Chaos is across-hyperparameter not within-run noise, so EMA can't help. Last principled lever exhausted. Champion (630) confirmed.

asi.hypothesis: EMA of model weights smooths the chaotic training trajectory -> smoother predictions -> less rollout drift
asi.finding: NEGATIVE. EMA decay 0.999 -> ED 9569 sharp 0.014 (BLANK): init contamination (0.999^2000=0.135, 13.5% of EMA is untrained random init). decay 0.99 -> ED 651 (parity/slightly worse than 630). decay 0.995 -> ED 684 (worse). EMA is parity-to-worse across all usable decays.
asi.why_ema_fails_here: EMA helps when training has within-run SGD noise (averages many noisy steps). But this benchmark's 'chaos' is ACROSS-hyperparameter sensitivity, not within-run noise - the training is DETERMINISTIC. Averaging weights of a deterministic trajectory just lags it; doesn't find a better minimum. The good solution at 630 isn't a noisy version of a better one - it IS the solution.
asi.conclusion: EMA is the last principled lever - now exhausted all: corruption types/targets, sampling, training stabilizers (warmup, EMA, velocity-clamp), generalization. Champion manifold_noise (630) is the confirmed optimum. No remaining non-overfitting directions.

description: RESOLVED: inference-time corruption HURTS (ED 7610 vs 630 decoupled). Confirms decoupled clean-inference extends to manifold_noise (model handles degradation, doesn't require it). All principled levers now exhausted including this last one. Champion (630, decoupled) confirmed.

asi.hypothesis: manifold_noise model was TRAINED on degraded context, so applying the same corruption at INFERENCE would match the training distribution and help
asi.finding: RESOLVED - decoupled clean inference is CORRECT for manifold_noise too. MANIFOLD_INFER=1 -> ED 7610 sharp 0.38 (blurry), much worse than decoupled 630. At inference the rolled-out last frame is ALREADY the model's degraded output; adding training-corruption on top DOUBLE-DEGRADES it -> blank. The model learned to HANDLE degradation, not REQUIRE it.
asi.principle_confirmed: Decoupled clean-inference (feed clean context at inference even though trained on corrupted) extends to manifold_noise. Previously only established for noise-aug in hypersphere work. Train on degraded context, infer on clean - the model corrects for the degradation it sees, it doesn't need it injected again.
asi.status: Now genuinely exhausted ALL principled levers: corruption type/target, sampling order, all training stabilizers, EMA, AND inference-time corruption. No remaining non-overfitting hypotheses. Champion manifold_noise (630, decoupled) confirmed.

description: BREAKTHROUGH (user idea): 3D-conv context encoder + in-network context-LATENT blur. ED=171 (3.7x better than champion 630!), ed_late 207, sharp 1.09. Feature-space context corruption >> input-space blur. 3D arch alone=2930; +latent blur=171.

asi.hypothesis: USER IDEA: replace channel-concat 2D model with a 3D-conv context encoder (explicit temporal axis), then blur the CONTEXT LATENT in feature space INSIDE the network (not input pixels)
asi.finding: BREAKTHROUGH. 3D arch alone (no corruption): ED 2930 sharp 0.99 - already beats 2D none (5622, sharp 0.55); the temporal inductive bias alone stabilizes rollout. 3D + LATENT_BLUR=0.7 (in-network feature-space context blur): ED 171, ed_late 207, sharp 1.09 - 3.7x better than previous champion (630)! 17x better than 3D-alone.
asi.why_latent_blur_wins: Input-space blur (manifold_noise) corrupts raw pixels including low-level texture the early layers need. IN-NETWORK latent blur corrupts the context's HIGH-LEVEL learned features (position/shape) - exactly what drifts during AR rollout - while preserving low-level structure. More on-manifold at the relevant abstraction level. Plus the 3D conv gives a natural isolated context latent to corrupt (impossible in channel-concat arch).
asi.combined_with: 3D temporal conv (better dynamics extrapolation) + feature-space context corruption. Both contribute: 3D alone 2930, +latent blur 171.
asi.applicability: Directly relevant to user's 4ctx->3fut weather model: use a 3D/temporal conv over the 4 context frames, and blur that context representation in feature space during training.

description: FALSE OUTLIER confirmed: latent blur 0.7=171 but neighbors 0.5/0.6/0.8=4271/4307/4632, randomized=5497. Knife-edge, not robust. Run #75 (171) was a chaotic lucky spike. Honest correction. Real finding: 3D-conv arch is robustly more stable (2930 vs 2D 5622) but worse than 2D+manifold_noise (630); doesn't combine with input corruption (21138).

Randomizing sigma [0.35,1.05] -> 5497 (averages into the bad region). The 171 was a chaotic knife-edge lucky point, NOT a robust effect. A real basin would have good neighbors; this is an isolated spike.
asi.correcting_record: Run #75 (ED 171, 'BREAKTHROUGH') is a FALSE OUTLIER - the exact pattern the prior FINDINGS warned about. Not trustworthy. The robust champion remains 2D manifold_noise (630).

BUT 3D-alone ED (2930) is still worse than 2D+manifold_noise (630). (2) 3D + input manifold_noise = catastrophic (21138) - techniques don't combine; input corruption is mismatched to the 3D arch.
asi.user_idea_verdict: Creative and well-motivated (corrupt high-level context features), but in this chaotic toy the in-network latent blur is a knife-edge, not robust. Worth re-testing in a less chaotic setup (bigger model, gentler LR) where the chaos doesn't dominate - the PRINCIPLE (feature-space corruption) may still be sound.

asi.finding: NEGATIVE. LATENT_DROPOUT=0.05 -> ED 3001 (same as 3D-alone 2930, no gain); 0.2 -> ED 5088 (worse). The high train_loss (1.8) is just dropout inflating training loss, not divergence (eval fine). Dropout doesn't help.

Neither robustly beats 3D-alone (2930). The 3D-conv architecture itself is the only robust sub-finding (better temporal bias, prevents blur failure) but its ED (2930) is worse than the 2D+manifold_noise champion (630).

The corruption just adds noise to an already-stable representation. On the 2D arch, the drift is in PIXEL space (blurry outputs) so input-space corruption works; on the 3D arch the failure mode differs (position drift, ED 2930) and isn't fixed by feature corruption.

asi.finding: PARTIAL but not enough. 3D + mild input (blur 0.2, jitter 0.05, LAST_ONLY) -> ED 788 sharp 1.03 train_loss 0.26 (stable, unlike the strong 0.5/0.20 which gave 21138). Better than 3D-alone (2930) but WORSE than 2D champion (630). ed_late 6108 (bad - position drift accumulates late in rollout).

Input corruption partially fixes it (788) but not enough to beat 2D+manifold (630). The 2D channel-concat + input manifold_noise remains the robust optimum - the input corruption is better matched to the 2D arch's pixel-space drift.

NONE beat 2D+manifold_noise (630). 3D arch is a real sub-finding (better temporal bias, prevents blur) but doesn't combine to win. Champion unchanged: 2D manifold_noise 630.

description: NEW CHAMPION: SAMPLE_AVG=4 (average 4 noise-sample endpoints per AR step). ED=451 (was 630), ed_late 460 (was 789). Robust variance reduction (N=8->465 confirms basin, not knife-edge). Inference-only, cheap (+2s), no retraining, applies to any RF forecaster. Combined with manifold_noise training corruption.

asi.hypothesis: Average N noise-sample endpoints per AR rollout step -> reduce per-step prediction variance -> less drift compounding
asi.finding: ROBUST WIN. SAMPLE_AVG=4 -> ED 451, ed_late 460 (champion N=1 was 630/789). 28% better ED, 42% better ed_late. Barely slower (74s vs 72s - the 24 rollouts x 4 samples = 96 processed in one batch). VERIFIED ROBUST: N=8 -> ED 465 (same basin, not a knife-edge). N=4 is the sweet spot (diminishing returns).
asi.why_it_works: Rectified flow maps noise z0 -> endpoint. On deterministic Lorenz dynamics the model SHOULD map any z0 to the same next-frame, but in practice different z0 yield slightly different endpoints (model/sampling variance). That variance COMPOUNDS over AR steps. Averaging N endpoints per step reduces the variance -> less compounding drift. Mathematically a variance reducer -> robust & monotonic (unlike the latent-blur knife-edge).
asi.applicability: Inference-only, no retraining, applies to ANY rectified-flow/diffusion forecaster including the user's 4ctx->3fut weather model. Cheap. Combine with manifold_noise training corruption. New champion: 2D manifold_noise + SAMPLE_AVG=4 = ED 451, sharp 1.11.
asi.robustness: N=4 (451) and N=8 (465) both in the ~450-465 basin - genuine effect, not chaos. sharp 1.11 (slightly artifacty but acceptable, not blurry).

description: SAMPLE_AVG sweep complete: N=1->630, N=2->496, N=4->451 (sweet spot), N=8->465. Textbook variance-reduction curve, robust. Champion = SAMPLE_AVG=4 (ED 451).

asi.complete_picture: Averaging is a clean, robust, principled win. Champion = SAMPLE_AVG=4 (ED 451). The curve confirms it's genuine variance reduction (not a knife-edge like latent-blur was).

asi.finding: NEGATIVE. NOISE_INJECT=0.5 + SAMPLE_AVG=4 -> ED 473, slightly WORSE than champion 451. Stochastic re-noising adds noise that averaging can't fully remove. Deterministic Euler + averaging > stochastic sampling.

asi.finding: GENERALIZATION CONFIRMED. SEED=2: full champion ED 6579 (sharp 0.58, train_loss 0.35). Beats manifold_noise-alone on seed-2 (9659) and none (12867). Averaging added ~32% on seed-2, consistent with ~28% on seed-0 -> seed-invariant benefit, as predicted (averaging is inference variance reduction, independent of training seed).

asi.finding: PARTIAL: averaging DID rescue ODE=48 from chaos (1161->476, confirming the ODE chaos was sampling-variance amplification). But 476 is still slightly worse than ODE=32+AVG=4 (451). ODE=32 remains the sweet spot even with averaging.

Only better dynamics learning (fails in this toy: 3D arch worse, multi-step loss unstable, EMA/warmup fail) or self-feed (user can't) could reduce it. This is the floor for no-self-feed techniques on this benchmark.

No remaining principled no-self-feed hypothesis with real prior. Champion = manifold_noise + ODE32 + SAMPLE_AVG4 = 451.

description: NEGATIVE: residual-bank corruption fails. resbank a=1.0->1133, a=0.3->1996 (both worse than 451). Model residual isn't position-independent (has position error + noise) -> real+residual = artifacts. Confirms systematic-bias floor is fundamental for no-self-feed. Champion unchanged (451).

asi.hypothesis: Bank the model's (pred-truth) error RESIDUALS (~position-independent bias structure) and apply to real frames -> real+residual looks like a model output at correct position -> targets systematic-bias floor, no two-blob
asi.finding: NEGATIVE. resbank RES_ALPHA=1.0 -> ED 1133 (train_loss 0.93, over-corrupts); 0.3 -> ED 1996 (non-monotonic, worse). Both much worse than champion 451, blurry (sharp 0.77-0.79).
asi.why_it_fails: The model's residual is NOT position-independent - it contains per-frame position error (blob slightly displaced) + sample_step noise. real+residual at a different position = misalignment/artifacts, not a clean bias emulation. Plus the bank mixes residuals from different training stages (bias drifts).
asi.conclusion: This was the most principled remaining idea for the systematic-bias floor. Its failure CONFIRMS the floor is fundamental for no-self-feed techniques: you cannot cleanly capture/emulate the model's evolving bias without live closed-loop self-correction (self-feed). Static generic corruption (manifold_noise) + variance reduction (averaging) is the ceiling. Champion unchanged: 451.
asi.space_definitively_exhausted: Every principled no-self-feed lever now tested: training corruptions (manifold_noise optimal), full inference-sampling space, 3D arch + feature corruption, multi-step loss, EMA/warmup/clamp, residual-bank. No remaining hypothesis with real prior.

description: Lever-interaction test: jitter=0.16+averaging -> ED 736 (worse than j0.20+averaging 451). Levers are SYNERGISTIC (averaging rewards stronger corruption), not redundant. Champion (j0.20+AVG4=451) is the confirmed joint optimum. Don't reduce corruption when adding averaging.

asi.finding: NO - levers are SYNERGISTIC, not redundant. jitter=0.16 + averaging -> ED 736, much worse than jitter=0.20 + averaging (451). Without averaging, j0.16 (824) ~= j0.20 (739); WITH averaging, j0.20 (451) >> j0.16 (736). Averaging REWARDS the stronger corruption. The champion (j0.20 + SAMPLE_AVG=4) is the confirmed JOINT optimum.
asi.transferable_insight: The two levers operate on DIFFERENT failure modes (corruption=context mismatch; averaging=sampling variance) so they don't substitute - they stack, and the strongest corruption+averaging combo is best. For the user: use BOTH at their individually-optimal settings; don't reduce corruption when adding averaging.
asi.space_confirmed_exhausted: 31 experiments. Every principled lever tested including this interaction. Champion manifold_noise(j0.20) + ODE32 + SAMPLE_AVG4 = 451 is the definitive joint optimum. No remaining hypothesis.

description: CONFIRM embed-only is NEUTRAL (noise): re-run gave 1543 vs 1508. Within-session non-determinism ~2.3%. Power-norm corruption neutral-to-harmful on champion at all magnitudes/stages. Sharpness always drops, train_loss always rises. Pivoting to WCLAMP=50 regime.

asi.confirmation: Re-ran embed-only (identical config): ED 1543 vs first run 1508. WITHIN-SESSION NON-DETERMINISM ~2.3% (despite CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG + deterministic settings - torch.rand in corruption mask + residual GPU noise). The 1508 'improvement' was NOISE.
asi.noise_floor: ~2-3% within-session ED noise. Must see >5-6% improvement to trust. Baseline 1553, embed-only 1508/1543 (avg 1525) = within noise = NEUTRAL.
asi.conclusion_champion_regime: Power-norm corruption on well-calibrated WCLAMP=6 champion: two-stage HURTS (ED 1984), embed-only NEUTRAL (1525 vs 1553). Sharpness ALWAYS drops (0.81-0.82 vs 0.84), train_loss ALWAYS rises 4.5x. No beneficial config found on the champion.
asi.partial_vindication_stands: Power-norm sharpness hit (-3.6%) milder than old corruption (-8.4%) - the normalization DOES reduce blurring, but not enough to yield ED gain on a model that doesn't need the regularization.

asi.wclamp50_baseline_this_env: WCLAMP=50 no-aug AVG4 SEED=0 (current env): ED 4410, sharp 0.16, mass 0.73, train_loss 0.057. MUCH better than old env's 21636 - env shifted massively (confirms why old absolute numbers aren't reproducible).
asi.regime_character: WCLAMP=50 = blurry/degraded regime here: sharp 0.16 (vs WCLAMP=6's 0.84), mass 0.73 (vs 0.086). Model under-emphasizes t~=0 forecasting direction -> blurry mean-regressed rollout. This is the regime where corruption's regularization (force robustness to corrupted context) previously helped.
asi.next: Test power-norm two-stage corruption (PROB=0.3 EMBED=0.10 BLOCK0=0.05 = production defaults) at WCLAMP=50. Direct comparison to old corruption's SEED=0 win (old env 26104->23933). In THIS env baseline is 4410; if corruption < 4410 with sharpness UP, power-norm helps the undertrained regime.

description: WCLAMP=50 two-stage power-norm: ED 4410→1568 (-64%) BUT sharp FLAT 0.16, mass WORSE 0.79, train_loss 5x. METRIC-GAMING artifact (blur→pooled-feature mean regression). Sharpness+mass tell truth: no real gain. Corruption crudely mimics the WCLAMP=6 fix.

asi.finding: Power-norm two-stage at WCLAMP=50: ED 4410->1568 (-64%!) BUT sharpness FLAT (0.16->0.16), mass WORSE (0.73->0.79), train_loss 5x (0.057->0.27). This is the METRIC-GAMING artifact: ED improves because blurrier frames' pooled features regress toward reference mean, NOT real quality.
asi.truth_tellers: Sharpness (flat 0.16) and mass_drift (worse 0.79) reveal no real improvement. ED is fooled by mean regression. CONFIRMS prior session's warning: for the ViT, trust sharpness+mass, not ED, when corruption is active.
asi.profound_insight: Corruption at high-WCLAMP (blurry regime) partially mimics LOWERING WCLAMP (shifting toward t~=0 forecasting) but crudely + with metric-gaming. ED 1568 here is suspiciously close to the WCLAMP=6 baseline (1553) - corruption is a crude proxy for the clean WCLAMP=6 fix. The right lever is WCLAMP=6, not corruption.
asi.next: Test embed-only at WCLAMP=50 (blurs less at WCLAMP=6). If it raises SHARPNESS above 0.16 (real deblurring) with ED<4410, it's a genuine win. If sharpness stays 0.16, confirms all corruption here is metric-gaming.

description: DEFINITIVE metric-gaming: embed-only WCLAMP=50 ED 913 (<champion's 1553!) but sharp STUCK 0.16, mass 0.79. ED meaningless under corruption. Power-norm fails identically to old corruption. Final test: latent-dropout angle on champion.

asi.DEFINITIVE_metric_gaming: Embed-only at WCLAMP=50: ED 913 (BELOW the WCLAMP=6 champion's 1553!) yet sharpness STUCK 0.157, mass 0.79, train_loss 0.27. ED keeps dropping as corruption increases mean-regression, while sharpness/mass stay at degraded values. ED is COMPLETELY MEANINGLESS when corruption is active in the blurry regime.
asi.rule: When corruption is active, trust sharpness_ratio + mass_drift, NEVER rollout_ed. ED is fooled by blur->pooled-feature mean regression. This is the single most important methodological lesson.
asi.power_norm_vs_old_identical_failure: Power-norm corruption fails identically to old global mean/std corruption: neutral-to-hurt on well-calibrated model (WCLAMP=6), metric-gaming on blurry model (WCLAMP=50). The ONLY difference: power-norm blurs slightly less (sharpness hit -3.6% vs -8.4% on champion). Normalization geometry doesn't change the fundamental failure.
asi.next: Final test: 'corruption as latent dropout' (gentle+frequent: PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03 embed-only) on WCLAMP=6 champion. Rules out whether ANY power-norm config acts as a beneficial regularizer on a non-overfitting model.

description: BREAKTHROUGH candidate: latent-dropout corruption (PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03 embed-only) on champion → ALL metrics improve: ED 1441 (-7.2%), sharp UP 0.89, mass 0.057. Gentle+frequent=dropout regime (vs strong+sparse=blur). Confirming next.

asi.BREAKTHROUGH_candidate: 'Corruption as latent dropout' (PROB=0.7, EMBED=0.03, embed-only, WCLAMP=6): ALL metrics IMPROVE - ED 1553->1441 (-7.2%), sharpness UP 0.84->0.89 (SHARPER not blurrier!), mass 0.086->0.057 (-33%), ed_late 1759->1633. OPPOSITE of every prior corruption config.
asi.mechanism: Gentle+frequent corruption = latent dropout. Strong+sparse (PROB=0.3 EMBED=0.10) destroys info and blurs (sharp 0.81). Gentle+frequent (PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03) prevents over-reliance on single tokens -> spreads attention -> better generalization -> sharper rollout. This IS the user's 'uniform info spread' hypothesis, but it only works in the gentle+frequent (dropout) regime, not strong+sparse.
asi.vs_prior_embed_only: Prior embed-only PROB=0.3 EMBED=0.10: ED neutral 1508/1543, sharp DOWN 0.81. This PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03: ED down 1441, sharp UP 0.89. The LEVER is gentle+frequent (high PROB + low scale), exactly the dropout regime.
asi.real_not_metric_gaming: Sharpness UP + mass DOWN confirms REAL improvement, not blur-metric-gaming (which shows sharp flat/down + mass up).
asi.next: MUST confirm with re-run (noise floor ~2-3%; ED -7.2% is above but verify). Then sweep: vary PROB (0.5, 0.9) and EMBED (0.02, 0.05) to find optimum and verify SEED=2.

description: Confirm PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03: ED noisy (1441/1752, avg~baseline) but sharpness ROBUSTLY up (0.87-0.89 vs 0.84) and mass ROBUSTLY down (0.057-0.065 vs 0.086). Real quality gain; ED noisy from corruption RNG x chaos. Testing PROB=1.0 for lower variance.

asi.confirmation_result: Re-run PROB=0.7 EMBED=0.03: ED 1752 (vs first 1441; avg 1597 ~ baseline 1553). HIGH ED VARIANCE (+21% between runs) from corruption mask RNG x chaotic rollout amplification.
asi.robust_quality_gains: Sharpness ROBUSTLY up: 0.89, 0.87 (both > baseline 0.84, +5-6%). Mass ROBUSTLY down: 0.057, 0.065 (both < baseline 0.086, -24-33%). These are the trustworthy ViT metrics (prior session: sharpness/mass > ED). The corruption genuinely improves per-frame forecast QUALITY.
asi.mixed_picture: Primary metric ED is noisy/neutral (avg 1597 ~ 1553), but secondary quality metrics robustly improve. For AR-stability the ED measures positional distribution match (chaotic, noisy); sharpness/mass measure per-frame quality (stable). The corruption helps the latter robustly.
asi.variance_source: torch.rand corruption mask (per-sample) differs each run -> different trained model -> chaotic rollout amplifies small trajectory diffs -> large ED swings. To reduce: PROB=1.0 (always corrupt, removes mask RNG) or accept ED noise and trust sharpness/mass.
asi.next: Try PROB=1.0 EMBED=0.03 (consistent corruption, lowest mask-variance). If ED robustly < baseline with sharpness up, clean win. Also consider EMBED=0.05 (slightly stronger reg) at PROB=0.7.

description: Noise-floor established: no-corruption baseline ED 1553→1825 (+17.5%, train_loss stable). ED noise is inherent to chaotic rollout, not corruption. Single-run ED unreliable. Gentle corruption mean ED 1595 < baseline 1689 but within noise; sharpness/mass tend better.

asi.CRITICAL_noise_floor_finding: No-corruption baseline re-run: ED 1553->1825 (+17.5%), but train_loss stable (0.0074-0.0075) and sharpness stable (0.836-0.844). The ~17% ED noise is INHERENT to the chaotic Lorenz rollout metric, NOT from corruption. Single-run ED comparisons are UNRELIABLE.
asi.reframe: Pooled gentle-corruption runs (PROB 0.7/1.0 EMBED 0.03): ED 1441,1752,1443,1744 -> mean 1595. Baseline: 1553,1825 -> mean 1689. Corruption mean is slightly BELOW baseline but within noise. Sharpness: corruption 0.867 vs baseline 0.84 (tendency up). Mass: corruption 0.065 vs baseline 0.080 (tendency down).
asi.honest_status: Gentle/frequent power-norm corruption shows a MODEST tendency to improve quality (sharpness/mass) and is slightly below baseline ED on average, but the benchmark's ±17% ED noise makes it impossible to confirm a clean win. It is the SAFE variant (doesn't hurt); strong/sparse clearly hurts.
asi.implication_for_loop: Cannot reliably optimize ED via single runs. Sharpness is the only stable metric. For production recommendation: gentle+frequent (PROB>=0.7 EMBED~0.03 embed-only) is safe and may slightly help; validate on real data where the metric may be less noisy.
asi.next: Probe EMBED=0.05 (slightly stronger gentle) for a more robust quality signal, then write up findings.

description: 2k trajectories @ BATCH=96/4500 steps UNDERTRAINS: ED 2543 (worse than 220's ~1689), train_loss 0.014 vs 0.0075. 9× data, same compute → 2.8 epochs vs 25. Need bigger batch/more steps. Testing BATCH=256 next.

asi.finding: 2k @ BATCH=256: ED 1258 (looks better) BUT sharp 0.77 (worse than 220's 0.84), mass 0.115 (worse), train_loss 0.029 (vs 0.0075). This is the BLUR/UNDERTRAINING artifact: undertrained model regresses to mean -> lower ED via pooled-feature mean-regression, but sharpness/mass reveal WORSE quality. Trust sharpness/mass.
asi.2k_not_benchmarkable: 2k needs ~9x compute to converge (156k windows vs 17k). At fixed/2.7x budget it undertrains -> blurry -> ED metric-games. Fully converging needs ~12-26 min/run. Impractical for the fast loop. The 2k 'ED improvement' at both BATCH=96 (2543) and BATCH=256 (1258) is NOT real - it's undertraining blur.

For clean augmentor research: revert to 220-traj champion (well-trained, sharp 0.84, trustworthy metrics). Will validate augmentor on 2k only if it shows real promise on 220 (then a 12-min validation run is justified).

description: Learned adversarial augmentor (eps=0.05) HURTS: sharp 0.63, mass 0.22, ED 2248. Adversary attacks blob POSITION (highest-loss direction in position-critical task) → divergence. Same root cause as manifold_noise. Input-space adversarial unsuitable here.

asi.result: Learned adversarial augmentor (learned_adv, eps=0.05, warmup=500, 220-traj champion): ED 2248, sharp 0.63 (vs 0.84), mass 0.22 (vs 0.086), train_loss 0.045 (vs 0.0075). HURTS on every quality metric.
asi.KEY_mechanism: For a POSITION-CRITICAL forecasting task, the adversary's worst-case input perturbation attacks the BLOB POSITION first (position is the highest-loss direction). The model then cannot trust the context position -> positional divergence. SAME root cause as manifold_noise's positional divergence (prior session: input perturbation hurts ViT ED via position loss).
asi.fundamental_limitation: Input-space adversarial robustness training is unsuitable for position-critical forecasting: the adversary will always attack position (the easy high-loss target), which is the one thing the model must preserve. Sensor-noise robustness (texture) is a different, weaker target the adversary ignores in favor of position.
asi.cost: Adversarial 2-step training ~2x cost: 284s vs ~165s baseline (within budget edge).
asi.gan_instability_adds: Adversary LR 1e-3 vs model LR 1e-4 (10x faster) -> adversary dominates. Even if balanced, the position-attack is fundamental.
asi.next: Test high-freq-CONSTRAINED adversary (high-pass filter delta so it can ONLY attack texture/amplitude, not position = realistic sensor noise). If that also fails, input-space adversarial is definitively unsuitable here.

description: Texture-constrained adversary (hp=2.5): sharp 0.33, mass 0.49 — WORSE than unconstrained (0.63). Constraining to texture attacks texture (=sharpness) directly. Every adversarial direction the model needs → always hurts. Input-space adversarial = robustness-accuracy tradeoff, OOD for clean inference. Direction DEAD.

asi.result: Texture-CONSTRAINED adversary (ADV_HP=2.5 high-pass, eps=0.05): ED 5412, sharp 0.33, mass 0.49, train_loss 0.048. WORSE than unconstrained (sharp 0.63) AND baseline (0.84).
asi.counterintuitive_mechanism: Constraining the adversary to high-frequency makes it attack TEXTURE directly - and texture IS what sharpness measures. So the texture adversary collapses sharpness HARDER (0.33) than the position adversary (0.63). After high-pass + power-norm, eps energy concentrates in few high-freq pixels -> strong per-pixel texture noise -> model loses sharpness.
asi.DEFINITIVE_negative: Every attackable direction (position OR texture) is a direction the ViT needs. There is NO safe adversarial direction for a position+texture-critical forecasting task. Input-space adversarial robustness training is fundamentally unsuitable here.
asi.root_cause: Classic robustness-accuracy tradeoff: the adversarial WORST-CASE input is out-of-distribution for CLEAN inference (rollout uses clean/decoupled context). Training on OOD-hard examples degrades performance on the actual inference distribution. Pure cost, no benefit. The adversary's best case (disabled) = neutral = no-aug.
asi.gan_lr_imbalance_secondary: Adversary LR 1e-3 (10x model LR 1e-4) lets the adversary dominate - but even balanced, the OOD-worst-case issue is fundamental.
asi.direction_dead: Learned adversarial augmentor (both unconstrained and texture-constrained) FAILS. Combined with the latent-corruption negatives this session: robustness/augmentation mechanisms do not help this well-calibrated ViT. The found levers (WCLAMP=6, fp32, AVG4, ODE32) stand. Remaining gap to conv is inductive-bias/data-scale.

description: JIT_PATCH_HW=8 WIN: 48 tokens vs 192 → sharp 0.93 (vs 0.84, +10.7%), mass 0.024 (vs 0.086, −72%), ED 1512. Less overfitting on 220 traj (prior hypothesis verified). Capacity axis, not perturbation tax = why it works where all aug failed.

asi.WIN: JIT_PATCH_HW=8 (48 tokens vs 192) at champion config: ED 1512, SHARP 0.93 (vs 0.84 baseline, +10.7%), MASS 0.024 (vs 0.086, -72%), train_loss 0.0085. All metrics improve or hold.

Operates on capacity/overfitting axis, NOT a perturbation tax (why it works where all augmentation failed).

Qualitatively different from the ED-noise false positives (gentle corruption) - those improved only the noisy ED while sharp/mass degraded; here sharp/mass IMPROVE.

Direction unanimous; magnitude seed-dependent (SEED=0 wins sharp/mass most, SEED=2 wins ED most). PATCH_HW=8 is a ROBUST win.

asi.SEED2_verification_MIXED: 800k + PATCH_HW=8 at SEED=2: ED 805 (confirms big ED win: 803 S0 / 805 S2, both ~half of 170k), BUT sharp 0.86 + mass 0.081 - WORSE than 170k/PATCH_HW=8 at SEED=2 (sharp 0.90, mass 0.056).
asi.overfitting_discipline_catches_seed_spec: The 800k sharpness win (1.03 at S0) does NOT cleanly generalize: at S2 mass drift regresses (0.081 vs 170k 0.056) - the trustworthy signal. 800k trades mass/dynamics-accuracy for ED/sharpness at S2.

asi.robust_conclusion: PATCH_HW=8 is the ROBUST win (all metrics both seeds at 170k). 800k capacity is a NET ED/sharpness win but seed-dependent mass regression - monitor mass per-seed in production. 170k/PATCH_HW=8 is the mass-robust alternative.

asi.collapses_FINDING: Uniform-weighted x-pred (user's reference 'v-loss') COLLAPSES on this easy benchmark: train_loss 0.0011(ivar)->0.000038(uniform), sharp 0.95->1.18 (ARTIFACTS), mass 0.040->0.072, ED 1103->1363. The model ignores z_t and predicts y from CONTEXT alone (single-blob Lorenz data is easy enough that context determines the target).
asi.why_user_ref_works_there_not_here: User's uniform v-loss works on production data (multi-channel sat+lightning: context alone CANNOT determine the target -> no collapse). On this easy single-blob benchmark, context IS sufficient -> collapse. The 1/(1-t)^2 / 1/c_t^2 weighting exists precisely to PREVENT this collapse by forcing z_t usage at the data end.
asi.mechanism: Plain unweighted x-pred MSE -> trivial 'predict the condition' solution (documented in hypersphere_bridge_experiment.py docstring too). Low train_loss here is the collapse signature, not good fit.
asi.fix: Implement the CORRECT bridge v-loss: ||v_theta - u_t||^2 = (x_pred-y)^2 (1 - t c'/c)^2 clamped. This is a ONE-SIDED data-end upweight (like RF's 1/(1-t)^2) -> prevents collapse, is a genuine velocity loss, and is the bridge analog of the working RF velocity loss. Distinct from ivar (1/c_t^2, upweights BOTH endpoints incl. wasteful noise end) and uniform (collapses).

The clean-landing benefit dominates; less mid noise = less blur = better mass/sharpness.
